eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent marine layer and strong onshore flow from the Pacific are anchoring San Francisco’s June 8 high near the mid-60s, aligning with trader consensus on the 64–67 °F brackets. Early-June climatology shows average highs around 68 °F, but recent trough passages and enhanced westerly winds have suppressed daytime warming while promoting coastal stratus that limits solar heating. Official National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs indicate modest day-to-day variability driven by the exact timing of marine-layer clearing; a slightly stronger onshore component or lingering fog would cap the high at 64–65 °F, whereas brief afternoon sun could nudge readings into the upper 60s. Resolution hinges on the official daily maximum recorded at downtown or airport stations, with new model guidance expected overnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from meteorological agencies points to daytime maxima in Kuala Lumpur on June 9 clustered near 31–32 °C, producing nearly equal market-implied odds for those two outcomes amid typical early-June variability. Southeast Asia’s transition toward weak El Niño conditions favors slightly above-normal temperatures through enhanced subsidence and reduced cloud cover, yet local sea-surface temperatures near 30 °C and frequent afternoon convection introduce day-to-day fluctuations of 1–2 °C. Historical June climatology shows average highs of 32 °C with a standard deviation near 1.5 °C, while short-range ensemble guidance highlights sensitivity to steering winds and rainfall timing that can suppress peak readings. Updated forecasts expected within 48 hours will likely refine the balance between the leading outcomes.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from PAGASA place Manila's June 9 high near 32°C amid the onset of the southwest monsoon, with 30–40% rain chances that could moderate afternoon peaks through cloud cover and showers. Historical June averages hover around 32°C, though urban heat effects and variable convective timing introduce uncertainty between 32–34°C. Trader consensus favoring 33°C and 34°C reflects these narrow margins, where slight shifts in timing of precipitation or insolation could determine whether the daily maximum exceeds or falls short of the 33°C threshold. Updated model runs and daily PAGASA briefings in the next 48 hours will provide the clearest resolution signals.
